supporting.title: Föreskrifter om Skurugata naturreservat i Eksjö kommun

officialSources.officialDescriptionSummary: HÖ1 starts at Västra Lägern where Anebyleden and Östgötaleden meet Höglandsleden. The stage passes Munkebo, Hästemålen and Stengöl, follows parts of the old narrow-gauge railway, and ends at Skuruhatt beside Skurugata nature reserve.
officialSources.appDetailTextDraft: This short connector stage links Västra Lägern with the Höglandsleden junction at Skuruhatt. From the lake and the Anebyleden/Östgötaleden connection, the route heads south through quiet forest and cultural landscape, passing Munkebo, the old railway bridge and mill remains at Hästemålen, and Stengöl säteri before reaching Skuruhatt. The endpoint has strong visitor facilities and immediate access to Skurugata, but the gorge itself is rougher and more slippery than the blue HÖ1 rating suggests.

end.label: Skuruhatt
end.notes: Endpoint is the HÖ1/HÖ2/HÖ17 junction at the Skuruhatt/Skurugata visitor area.

officialGeometry.notes: No segment breaks or obvious endpoint gaps found in the official GPX.

start.distanceBasis: straight-line; official access page says about 1.5 km north along road 134
start.caveats: Rural service; verify exact travel date. Östgötaleden notes road walking can be avoided via a gravel road toward Katebo.

start.distanceBasis: straight-line; official access page says about 2 km west on road 134 or about 2.5 km via Smålandsleden/Anebyleden
start.caveats: Rural service; verify exact travel date. Stop appears in GTFS/JLT sources but was not found in the OSM stop query used by the transit lane.

end.distanceBasis: straight-line from Skuruhatt ledentré; practical walking route will be longer
end.caveats: Closest useful scheduled bus point found in the transit lane, but no official trailhead connector was found. Björnshult is nearly tied at about 6.19 km.

end.distanceBasis: straight-line from Skuruhatt ledentré; Länsstyrelsen describes road access from Eksjö as about 8 km
end.operatorNetwork: Jönköpings Länstrafik / regional rail and bus hub
end.caveats: Robust service hub, but trailhead access likely needs taxi, bicycle, car drop, or a planned road/walking route.

parking.name: Västra Lägern
parking.caveats: Parking is possible by the lake, but Östgötaleden warns there is no parking sign.

parking.name: Skurugata Naturreservat / Skuruhatt
parking.caveats: Länsstyrelsen describes signposted car access from Eksjö and route 40. Overnighting in vehicle, roof tent, or camper is prohibited in the reserve.

ferry.notes: No relevant ferry access found for this inland section.

facilities.description: HÖ1/A4/Östgötaleden junction at Västra Lägern. Parking is possible but not signed with a P sign.

waterSources.name: HÖ1 drinking water
waterSources.notes: No controlled drinking-water point was confirmed on HÖ1 or at the two endpoints. Carry water.

waterSources.name: Skurukälla
waterSources.notes: Visit Eksjö mentions Skurukälla as clear water in Skurugata, but no potable-water testing/control source was found. Do not import as potable without verification.

camping.notes: Do not treat Skuruhatt visitor facilities as a general free-camping area. In Skurugata nature reserve, tenting is allowed only at designated place and overnighting in vehicle, camper, or rooftop tent is prohibited.

shelter.notes: Hästemålen vindskydd appears on or near HÖ1 and should be imported with OSM-supplemented coordinate confidence. Skurugata has roofed rest shelters near the endpoint spur, but they are not confirmed as overnight shelters.

fire.notes: Skurugata reserve allows fires only at prepared fire sites using brought or provided wood. Länsstyrelsen showed a fire-risk advisory for Jönköpings län on 2026-04-29 but the Eksjö fire-ban query returned no active fire ban; do not import live fire-ban state as durable data.

protectedAreas.name: Skurugata
protectedAreas.notes: HÖ1 ends at/near the Skurugata reserve visitor area. Attach reserve-specific restrictions to the overlapping endpoint/reserve area unless later geometry confirms a longer overlap.

reserveRestrictions: No fires except at prepared fire sites with brought or provided wood.
No overnighting in motorhome, car, other vehicle, or rooftop tent.
Do not damage geological formations, living or dead trees, shrubs, or natural objects.
Do not collect mosses, lichens, or fungi except household edible mushrooms under the listed exceptions.

dogs.notes: No Skurugata-specific dog ban was found in the public reserve rules reviewed. General Swedish guidance still applies: from 1 March to 20 August dogs must be under extra control, and in practice are usually kept leashed; leash near grazing animals.

huntingAndLivestock.notes: No HÖ1-specific hunting closure was found. Add a general current-signage advisory for hunting season and agricultural/grazing land: do not disturb hunting, leash dogs near livestock, and close gates.

hazards.name: Skurugata gorge detour
hazards.notes: The Skurugata gorge/top area is rougher than HÖ1's blue rating: rocky/boulder terrain, slippery stone after rain, humidity/cold, and lingering snow/ice possible into spring or early summer. The accessible route from parking to Skuruhatt is easier.

currentClosures.notes: No current HÖ1 closure or reroute notice was found on the official HÖ1, Eksjö municipality, or Skurugata pages. Adjacent HÖ2 has a reroute note before Hässleåsa gård, which matters when continuing beyond Skuruhatt.

conditionReports.summary: Recent Skurugata-area reviews report good signposting and facilities, but emphasize that the gorge can be slippery and more difficult than an easy route rating suggests.
conditionReports.importImpact: Use only as endpoint/side-detour condition context, not as direct HÖ1 route condition.

conditionReports.summary: Komoot route/highlight context also treats the nearby Skurugata/Skuruhatt walks as moderate and needing sure-footedness.

conditionReports.source: Utsidan album for adjacent Höglandsleden Eksjö-Mariannelund
conditionReports.summary: Adjacent Höglandsleden report described the trail as in good condition, well-marked, and easy to follow.
conditionReports.importImpact: Older adjacent-stage context; do not use as current HÖ1 condition evidence.

conditionReports.summary: Older review noted sometimes poor markings and boggy/soggy stretches after heavy rain on a Mariannelund-Eksjö walk.
conditionReports.importImpact: Stale context only; not a HÖ1 currentness signal.

sourceContradictions.details: Smålandsleden/Naturkartan/Visit Eksjö describe Skuruhatt as 337 m above sea level, while Länsstyrelsen says 334 m above sea level.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Low. Avoid importing exact elevation unless resolved against authoritative geodata.

sourceContradictions.details: HÖ1 page and Visit Eksjö say the gorge is about 800 m; Naturkartan's Skurugata text says about 1 km.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Low. This is side-detour context, not HÖ1 section distance.

sourceContradictions.details: Some trail pages refer to Skuruhatt naturreservat, while the official protected area record is Skurugata, NVR 2002309.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Medium. Use Skurugata as the protected-area name; keep Skuruhatt for viewpoint/trailhead labels.

sourceContradictions.details: SityTrail has an older 'Höglandsleden: Delsträcka 5, Klinten - Västra Lägern' of 5 km, created/updated in 2022. This does not match current official HÖ1 7.5 km Västra Lägern-Skuruhatt.
sourceContradictions.importImpact: Medium. Ignore older sectioning for current HÖ1 import; use current Smålandsleden/Naturkartan stage page and GPX.

agents.result: Confirmed official section metadata, endpoints, primary sources, Skurugata reserve identity/rules, and source contradictions.
Confirmed official GPX direction, 158-point geometry, computed distance, no obvious gaps, and OSM composite relation notes.
Collected Västra Lägern, Munkebo, Hästemålen, Skuruhatt and Skurugata facility records with coordinates and import recommendations.
Identified Arvebo and Måletorpet for Västra Lägern access; identified Krösenlund and Eksjö station as weaker Skuruhatt-area public transport options; confirmed no ferry.
Found no current HÖ1 closure, gathered Skurugata/Skuruhatt condition context, and flagged stale route-app/older report conflicts.
Confirmed Skurugata restrictions, current fire-risk vs fire-ban distinction, dog/hunting/livestock advisories, and no HÖ1 closure found.

researchIterations.synthesisDecision: Strong enough for research-ready candidate normalization with caveats around Skuruhatt public-transport access, protected-area overlap extent, and facility deduplication.

openQuestions.question: Should Skurugata endpoint facilities about 400-460 m from HÖ1 be modeled as HÖ1 endpoint facilities, spur facilities, or separate protected-area facilities?
openQuestions.suggestedNextStep: During normalization, model them as endpoint/spur facilities and avoid implying they lie directly on the HÖ1 GPX.

openQuestions.question: Is there a better official or practical public-transport connection for Skuruhatt than Krösenlund/Björnshult/Eksjö station?
openQuestions.suggestedNextStep: Re-check JLT journey planner and local taxi/bike/walking options before publishing access guidance.

openQuestions.question: Does Hästemålen vindskydd have an official Smålandsleden/Naturkartan facility object under a different slug?
openQuestions.suggestedNextStep: Search official facility endpoints or ask trail maintainer before final import; current coordinate is OSM-supplemented.

openQuestions.question: What is the precise Skurugata reserve overlap with HÖ1 geometry?
openQuestions.suggestedNextStep: Intersect GPX with NVR boundary during normalization; apply reserve restrictions to overlap/endpoint rather than the full stage if overlap is short.

caveats: End public transport access is weak and not tied to an official trail connector.
Several Skurugata endpoint facility records need deduplication during normalization.
Hästemålen shelter coordinate is OSM-supplemented and should be verified if possible.
Reserve restrictions should be spatially scoped after boundary intersection.
